title: The Prediction of Risk Factors and the Temporal Dynamics of Paternal Postpartum Depression.
summary:
Following the birth of a child, approximately 8-13% of new fathers experience a depressive episode 6 months postpartum, in the following referred to as paternal depression (PD). Up until now however, there is no clear-cut evidence on whether there are any signs potentially hinting at PD in the first weeks postpartum before an actual clinical diagnosis was made.
The following study will be conducted for a total time span of two years, with the aim of scrutinizing and pinpointing the risk factors of PD in a participant pool of 237 subjects. Fathers will be part of a 24-week observational period, where a number of clinical and psychological information, as well as testosterone levels will be obtained.  Here, the leading question will be whether PD could have been predicted beforehand based upon any given characteristics. Moreover, the study utilizes an app developed to examine daily activities of the participants, as a shift in social behavior may serve as a potential risk factor and thus, might allow for an early prediction of PD.
In addition to the latter, 20 fathers will be part of an fMRI study  aimed at investigating whether there are structural brain changes in fathers following the birth of the child. Further, the focus lies on determining when these changes potentially take place and whether they impact paternal bonding.

interventions.name:
In total, there are eight measurement timepoints during the 24-week observational period.
With regard to the fMRI-project, subjects will be scanned at six timepoints.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Men aged 18-45,whose partners have given birth in the last six days in the Gynecology and Obstetrics Clinic in the University Medical Center Aachen.
Exclusion criteria:
- current or former neurological or psychiatric disorder,
- anti-depressive or anti-psychotic medication,
- current substance abuse,
- morbid obesity (BMI> 35kg/m2),
- severe illness of the newborn (infantile brain damage, chromosome aberration(s), severe congenital deformities), premature birth (< 29. week of pregnancy),
- poor comprehension of the German language.

- MRI exclusion criteria: metal implants (screws, plates, etc.) stents, clips, braces and retainer, cardiac surgery, epilepsy, larger tattoos, as well as further commonly known contraindications of a MRI measurement.
